anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW address pin A0 (pin 1) is on the +3.3V net, while the other address pins A1 (pin 2), A2 (pin 3), A3 (pin 4), A4 (pin 5) and A5 (pin 24) are all on GND. The PCA9685 7-bit address is 0x40 + A-pin bits, so A0 high gives 0x41.
anomalies.expected: The specification lists the PCA9685PW I2C address as 0x40, which requires all address pins low. A0 should be tied to GND like the other address pins.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The PWM driver would respond at 0x41 instead of 0x40, so firmware addressing it at 0x40 gets no response and no servo/PWM outputs are driven.

anomalies.observed: The 3.3 V LDO output (REG2.OUT) is on the net '+3.3V', which feeds the sensors and PCA9685. The MCU and FCC pull-up/decoupling rail is a separate net '+3V3' with no regulator output on it. The MCU VDD pins (FCC1 pins 11, 27, 50, 75, 100; NAVC1 pins 19, 32, 48, 64) are not on either rail.
anomalies.expected: The LDO output feeds both the MCUs and the sensors as one 3.3 V rail, per the specification ('3.3 V LDO (MCUs + sensors)', '3V3 feeds both MCUs and all I2C sensor ICs').

evidence.quote: 3.3 V LDO (MCUs + sensors) | Hades (top sheet) | ST LD39200PU33R

anomalies.impact: The MCUs' core supplies are not tied to the regulator output and the +3V3 rail has no source, so the MCUs may not power up or may run from an unregulated or floating supply.
